headline: Andrew Coleman says Ansell is a compounder for patient investors but PE of 19.4x is not yet cheap enough to buy; hold if you own it
reasoning: Coleman frames Ansell as a classic slow-and-steady compounder with earnings and sales growing just above inflation, mid-to-high single digit ROE/ROC, and relatively stable earnings. The defensive label applies both to its investment characteristics and its barrier products. The key question is whether PE of 19.4x offers enough starting yield for long-term compounding returns — his view is probably not yet. He recommends holding if owned and waiting for Mr Market to offer a better entry point.
quote: In the case of Ansell, it is often called defensive, which is probably true in terms of both their investment profile, earnings and sales growing just faster than inflation, reasonable, but not particularly low debt, ROE and ROC and mid to high single digits. That's defensive. But it's also true in terms of the products they make. I mean, they're providing barrier products, whether that's as gloves or prophylactics, right? And so as a result, just like their products, owning Ansell is unlikely to give you a particularly nasty surprise or a wonderful gain. But if you can buy it at the right price, that compounding power growing just a little bit faster than inflation for decades at a time with relatively low risk that anything is going to materially change the business can be a wonderful investment. So the question now is just simply is a PE of 19.4 enough to give you that compounding gain? And I would say probably not yet. So hold if you have it, if not, there are better options.
episode_title: the call: Monday 1 June
